steps.action: The authors set the aim: use new detrital zircon data to constrain maximum sedimentation ages, provenance and Permian–Triassic paleogeography of the Tauern Window.
steps.quote: Maximum sedimentation ages and provenance are discussed, providing constraints on Permian–Triassic paleogeography of Alpine basement domains and adjacent crustal blocks.

steps.action: They state two published rival proposals for the Kaserer Formation: a conformable Cretaceous cover on the Hochstegen limestone, or an older Permian–Triassic sequence emplaced as an overthrust nappe.
steps.quote: The Kaserer metasedimentary rocks are overthrust as a nappe system.

steps.action: They sampled metasedimentary units of the Glockner Nappe, the Kaserer Nappe and the Riffler Basin, and one metaigneous rock at the Glockner thrust plane, as found in the field.
steps.quote: Samples were collected for coupled U–Pb and Lu–Hf LA-ICP-MS zircon analysis

steps.action: They separated zircons, imaged them by cathodoluminescence and analysed U–Pb and Lu–Hf by LA-MC-ICP-MS at São Paulo; procedures are in Supplementary Material 4 (not supplied).
steps.quote: Zircon analyses were performed using a Neptune multicollector inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometer (ICP-MS)

steps.action: They estimated maximum sedimentation ages from 206Pb/238U ages with three estimators (YDG, YGC1, YGC2), excluding grains younger than 210 Ma as Pb loss.
steps.quote: Maximum sedimentation ages for metasedimentary rocks were obtained following three approaches

steps.action: They compared the three estimators within each sample; they agree for KAS, TXQZTG, SMQZT, FMA and BSF but diverge strongly for MSBG and MKG.
steps.quote: Sample KAS shows a well-defined Guadalupian maximum sedimentation age, based on all parameters

steps.action: They described detrital age spectra (provenance peaks) for each sample from KDE plots (Fig. 4).
steps.quote: In terms of provenance, Paleozoic ages are clearly dominant, with main peaks at ca. 480–440 and 320–280 Ma.

steps.action: They obtained a concordia crystallization age for the TXRH orthogneiss protolith and described its inherited xenocrysts.
steps.quote: yield a concordia age of 267 ± 2 Ma for the timing of crystallization of the felsic orthogneiss protolith

steps.action: They reported εHf by age group: dominantly subchondritic values before ca. 290 Ma, and a broad, apparently bimodal spectrum from ca. 290 Ma to the Middle Triassic.
steps.quote: zircons with crystallization ages between the middle Cisuralian (ca. 290 Ma) and the Middle Triassic show a broad compositional spectrum

steps.action: They compared the KAS Guadalupian maximum age with the two proposals and with the Anisian correlation, inferring Late Permian to Early Triassic deposition and finding no evidence for a Cretaceous age.
steps.quote: The Guadalupian maximum sedimentation age of sample KAS is in line with correlations of the Kaserer Formation upper section with Anisian rocks

steps.action: They retained the nappe interpretation: a tectonic contact between the Hochstegen Marble and the Kaserer Formation, while saying a Cretaceous age cannot be completely ruled out.
steps.quote: a tectonic contact between the top of the Upper Jurassic Hochstegen Marble and the Kaserer Formation is assumed

steps.action: They supported the tectonic contact with independent field evidence (folding styles, sheared gypsum, conformable contact with Middle Triassic carbonates) and with the Late Triassic maximum age of the overlying MSBG sample.
steps.quote: [...] supported by field evidence, such as different folding styles and local sheared gypsum lenses at the contact

steps.action: They reassigned the Glockner Nappe metasediments (FMA) from the Wustkogel Formation to the Seidlwinkel Formation as slightly younger Triassic deposits, with the Pfiffkar Formation as an alternative.
steps.quote: the maximum deposition age indicates a more likely affinity with the Seidlwinkel Formation

steps.action: They checked the maximum ages against the fossil-based Oxfordian age of the overlying Hochstegen Marble and inferred protracted continental sedimentation followed by a Jurassic transgression.
steps.quote: The obtained late Permian–Triassic maximum deposition ages are also in agreement with the age of the Hochstegen Marble

steps.action: Faced with a surprisingly old (middle Permian) maximum age and a wide age spread in the Bündnerschiefer sample, they proposed an open, deep Penninic basin with an enlarged catchment.
steps.quote: The wide spread of zircon ages may be explained by the existence of a relatively open and deep Penninic Ocean basin

steps.action: They matched detrital age populations to published magmatic events (Variscan, Cenerian, Pan-African, Cadomian, north African cratons) to identify likely sources.
steps.quote: Late Carboniferous-Permian ages are attributed to Variscan and post-Variscan magmatism, which is well-documented in the Tauern Window

steps.action: Using provenance and published reconstructions, they placed the Tauern Window between the Austroalpine/South Alpine units, the External Massifs and the Bohemian Massif during the Permian–Triassic (Fig. 7).
steps.quote: the Tauern Window might have been placed between the Austroalpine and South Alpine units, External Alpine units and the Bohemian Massif

steps.action: They compared the presence and absence of Ordovician–Silurian and Stenian–Tonian sources across candidate domains, concluding that Austroalpine and South Alpine basement was a major detritus source.
steps.quote: is well documented in coeval Austroalpine and South Alpine sequences

steps.action: From the narrow age range, the structural position and Brenner base tunnel drilling results, they proposed a tectonic mélange zone formed on a hyperextended margin.
steps.quote: may represent a tectonic mélange zone, which originated on a distal and hyperextended continental margin

steps.action: They compiled their εHf data with published Austroalpine and South Alpine detrital and magmatic zircons (Fig. 8a) and linked the ca. 290 Ma isotopic change to the onset of intracontinental extension.
steps.quote: can be linked to the transition from the Variscan post-collisional stage to a generalized intracontinental extension

steps.action: They proposed lithospheric thinning with magmatic underplating as the mechanism mixing crustal and mantle sources to produce the Hf evolution.
steps.quote: Lithospheric thinning coupled with magmatic underplating might have triggered rifting-related magmatism and high-temperature/low-pressure metamorphism

steps.action: They kept the claim that the Tauern metasediments record the progressive transition from Variscan post-collisional processes to rifting and Penninic ocean opening.
steps.quote: late Permian–Triassic metasedimentary rocks of the Tauern Window monitor the progressive transition from Variscan collisional/post-collisional tectonomagmatic processes to intracontinental rifting

steps.action: They suggested that the anomalously young zircons, earlier set aside as Pb loss, may reflect a post-depositional hydrothermal overprint, and left this unresolved.
steps.quote: may indicate the existence of a post-depositional hydrothermal overprint

steps.action: They stated the final claims: Late Permian–Triassic maximum deposition ages, Kaserer deposition in the Late Permian–Early Triassic within a nappe, the Wustkogl-attributed rocks being Late Triassic, the ca. 290 Ma Hf change, and the paleogeographic position.
steps.quote: Deposition of the Kaserer Formation took place between the late Permian and the Early Triassic

tree.answer: Eight metasedimentary samples from several units give similar ages and Hf signatures
Mostly: three age estimators agree in most samples; field evidence and an overlying sample support the contact
Kept: Late Permian–Triassic ages; Kaserer as a nappe is the best explanation; Cretaceous not fully ruled out

end.claim: Detrital zircons from western Tauern Window metasediments give Late Permian to Triassic maximum deposition ages, indicating protracted sedimentation and magmatism from the Late Paleozoic into the Mesozoic.

decisive_move.sentence: Without the maximum sedimentation ages from the YDG, YGC1 and YGC2 estimators applied to the new U–Pb data, none of the stratigraphic, tectonic or paleogeographic reassignments would exist.

gates.evidence: Action: the sampling targets the units in the stated Kaserer controversy (§2 ¶2, §3 ¶1), but no hypothesis is said to have directed sample choice. Claim: a Cretaceous-age youngest zircon population would have supported the conformable-Cretaceous proposal, but a Permian maximum age cannot refute Cretaceous deposition, which the authors concede (§5.1 ¶1). Registration: nothing is reported as fixed before the data; the 210 Ma Pb-loss cutoff and the n = 2/3 cluster rules are stated without saying when they were fixed (§4.1 ¶1).

imports.item: Laser-ablation multicollector ICP mass spectrometry (Neptune MC-ICP-MS, Analyte G2 excimer laser)
Cathodoluminescence imaging to choose analysis sites
Kernel density estimation of age distributions (DensityPlotter)
CHUR reference values from unequilibrated chondrites (Bouvier et al. 2008) for εHf

novelty_claims.quote: new U–Pb and Lu–Hf detrital zircon data of Permian–Triassic metasedimentary sequences of the Tauern [...]

limits: Sub-claim statuses: the Kaserer Formation as a Late Permian–Early Triassic overthrust nappe is best_explanation, not confirmed; the authors say a Cretaceous age cannot be completely ruled out, and a maximum depositional age logically cannot exclude younger deposition (inference). The reassignment of the Wustkogel-attributed rocks (FMA) to the Seidlwinkel Formation is best_explanation, with the Pfiffkar Formation left open. The ca. 290 Ma Hf change marking the onset of extension, and the lithospheric thinning/underplating mechanism, are best_explanation ('possibly', 'might have'). The paleogeographic position is best_explanation, although the abstract says results 'confirm' it. The Bündnerschiefer middle Permian maximum age is left as an anomaly with a tentative explanation. The young (<210 Ma) zircons are first excluded as Pb loss and later suggested to reflect hydrothermal overprint, without resolution. Process gaps: analytical procedures, standards and reproducibility of reference materials are only in Supplementary Material 4, which was not supplied, so analytical reproduction checks cannot be coded. The field evidence for the tectonic contact is described briefly, not documented in detail. MKG has only 11 grains. The conclusions say the Kaserer Formation 'was overthrust by the Hochstegen Marble' (§6 ¶2), whereas §5.2 ¶5 has the Kaserer Formation thrust over the Hochstegen Marble; this internal inconsistency is not addressed. Reviewers are thanked in the acknowledgements, but no review file was supplied, so no review sequence is coded and changes made in review are unknown. Whether the field observations are new or come from the authors' earlier work (Veselá et al. 2008, 2011) is not stated (inference).

disagreements.support: The Guadalupian maximum age of KAS, the Anisian correlation, field evidence for a tectonic contact, and the Late Triassic maximum age of the overlying MSBG; a Cretaceous age is said not to be completely ruled out.
disagreements.quote: In contrast to previous proposals (e.g., Frisch 27; Thiele 78; Rockenschaub et al. 56; Schmid [...]

disagreements.target: Thiele 1976: attribution of the Tuxer Joch–Hintertux metaquartzites (FMA) to the Permian–Triassic Wustkogel Formation
disagreements.support: The Middle–Late Triassic maximum sedimentation ages of FMA match the Seidlwinkel Formation and MSBG, so the rocks are reassigned.
disagreements.quote: so far attributed to the Wustkogl Formation of the Central Tauern Window, are in fact Late Triassic

disagreements.target: Classical Jurassic–Cretaceous assignment of the Bündnerschiefer (Steinmann 1994; Garofalo 2012)
disagreements.support: Sample BSF gives only a middle Permian maximum age; the authors explain the age spread by a large catchment and do not reassign the unit.
disagreements.quote: though this unit has been classically assigned to the Jurassic-Cretaceous
